The \texttt{data-stat} attribute serves as a stable key for feature extraction, enabling consistent mapping across tables. The failure mode of bare shell requests returning 403 arises because same-origin policies block access until JS uncomments placeholders. This design enforces a dualism between static HTML and dynamic data, necessitating browser automation. The diagnostic features—such as OL/DL attribution, coverage splits, and referee environments—are derived from advanced table structures that encode tactical and behavioral signals. These features are then mapped into GSI’s Bayesian framework for inference and into GSE’s state transition engine for predictive modeling. The use of HTML comments for older Vegas lines introduces a parsing layer that must be robustly handled to avoid data loss. The legal unit of analysis includes diagnostic features like YBC/rush and draft capital, while illegal units such as direct coefficients are excluded to maintain model integrity.
